headline: Tumor-relative spatial expression patterns are mapped without cell segmentation
label: Spatial Tumor Pattern Analysis
summary: Recent preprints and a 2026 publication apply computational spatial and transcriptomic tests to tumor heterogeneity and patient-linked outcomes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational extraction of tumor-organized information from high-dimensional measurements rather than resolution of a single mechanism. TOASTER applies topological data analysis to continuous spatial protein expression in multiplexed spatial proteomics, avoiding cell segmentation, and tests association with patient outcome. SCOMV classifies genes and cell types by vectorial spatial relationships to tumor regions and identifies spatially differential genes. A published tumor scRNA-seq analysis reports that malignant cells group by patient tumor across 14 cancer types, with this identity encoded diffusely across the transcriptome. What is new is the shift from discrete cell-level calls toward continuous spatial and whole-transcriptome representations of tumor structure. All three items are computationally derived, and the two preprints remain unvalidated in the items provided.
